messages:
maria: heads up — the canary for the new per-key burst throttling (policy v2) started at 09:12 UTC and we're seeing an uptick in 429s from a handful of mid-tier customers. saw ~1.8% 429 rate vs baseline 0.1% in the first 15m. tagging @simon and @alex to triage

alex: seeing 3 fresh tickets flagged P2 from support. customers report sudden rate limit errors during short spikes (chat apps doing front-end burst). they have short lived bursts (~40 reqs in <10s).

simon: on it. quick question — was canary set to 5% of traffic or 5% of orgs?

maria: 5% of orgs via rollout flag `rate_limit_rollout=canary-2026-04-26`. policy applies per-api-key token bucket with burst_capacity=20 and refill=1/s (new defaults).

alex: repro steps from support: 
1) open connection and fire 40 normal completions in 8s
2) last ~10 calls get 429
3) if they pause 2s, tokens <recover> and some succeed

ben: from billing POV, this will reduce transient overages so wanted but customers expect tiny bursts. any mitigation short-term?

ops-bot: alert: canary 1761504321 - 5% rollout - 429_rate increased by +1.7% in eu-west-1.

simon: pulling logs now. grabbing request traces for one of the affected orgs (org_48f).

simon: quick log excerpt: 
```
[2026-04-26T09:17:04Z] org=org_48f req_id=abc123 status=429 reason=RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED tokens_left=0 bucket_cap=20
[2026-04-26T09:17:05Z] org=org_48f req_id=abc124 status=200 tokens_left=0
[2026-04-26T09:17:06Z] org=org_48f req_id=abc125 status=429 tokens_left=0
```

maria: ok that aligns with the policy. looks like burst_capacity=20 too low for some legitimate front-end bursts they do. the policy was intentionally conservative to reduce cost.

tasha: product note — a few established customers (SaaS chat vendors) do ephemeral bursts from client reconnects. we need to avoid breaking committed customers. can we do quick rollback for the canary and reopen with softer thresholds?

simon: we have two immediate options: 
- rollback the rollout flag for all canary orgs to v1 (safe, immediate)
- patch runtime to add a short grace window (sliding burst allowance) — takes ~40m to ship to canary.

maria: prefer rollback for speed. we'll update the rollout config and then iterate on a revised policy.

alex: if we rollback, support wants an automated message template to send to affected orgs explaining temporary step and ETA for follow-up.

maria: agreed. I'll flip the flag now. initiating rollback via deploy-bot.

deploy-bot: command received: rollback-rollout --flag rate_limit_rollout --target canary-2026-04-26 --to v1 --initiated-by maria
deploy-bot: rollback started (jobs queued). will report completion.

ops-bot: metric check starting: comparing 15m windows pre/post rollback.

simon: while that's running — can we capture the orgs list so support can message? alex, can you pull the 5% org ids and we'll add them to the incident message?

alex: pulling now, posting below: 
- org_48f
- org_7a2
- org_99b
- org_1c3

ben: billing question — do we need to credit those customers for failed requests? My suggestion: no automatic credit now; triage each on a case-by-case, but offer a goodwill token if they lost revenue.

tasha: agree with case-by-case. product to own comms template.

deploy-bot: rollback completed successfully at 09:42 UTC. rollout flag `rate_limit_rollout` set to `v1` for canary group.

ops-bot: post-rollback summary: 429_rate returned to baseline within 6m. summary: pre-rollback 429=1.9% -> post-rollback 0.12%. latency impact negligible.

simon: confirmed. logs show keys back to old bucket settings. creating a follow-up PR to propose policy v2.1 with increased burst_capacity=50 and a short grace period (100ms cooldown window per connection) — will include sim perf and estimated cost delta.

maria: action items: 
- @simon PR for v2.1 with sim numbers (ETA end of today)
- @tasha draft customer comms and share with support (ETA 60m)
- @alex send messages to listed orgs and flag cases as potential credits if revenue impact (ETA 30m)
- @ben hold off credits until review

alex: will send messages and attach repro instructions + workaround (throttle client backoff to 10 req/s bursts).

tasha: also need an internal postmortem note in incidents channel once we have PR and cost numbers. I'll draft skeleton.

maria: thanks team. lesson: canary thresholds need to model client burst patterns, not just avg QPS. we'll add traffic-shape sampling to canary criteria.

simon: +1. I'll add traffic-shape metrics to the canary dashboard (p50 burst size, p95 burst size) so next rollout is less surprise.

alex: customers replied to my first outreach — they appreciate the quick rollback and want to be looped on the re-roll. i'll cc them on follow-up. :thumbsup:

maria: closing the thread for now. re-open if the rollback shows lingering issues. thanks all.
